model: Reyrolle 7SR10 Argus overcurrent and earth-fault relay (Modbus RTU)
applies_to: Reyrolle 7SR10 overcurrent / earth-fault relays, default Modbus RTU point list per Communication Protocols manual C53000-L7040-C002-7 (edition 11.2025, V01.00).
summary: The 7SR10 is a compact non-directional overcurrent and earth-fault protection relay with an RS-485 port that can run IEC 60870-5-103, Modbus RTU or DNP3. Under Modbus, commands are coils, protection and status indications are discrete inputs, and measurands are input registers. This map covers the default point list: binary outputs, control commands, protection elements, voltages, currents, frequency, power factor, maximum demand, fault values, counters and status bit strings.

addressing.note: The point list uses Modicon numbers: coils 00001+, inputs 10001+, input registers 30001+. Subtract the block base for the wire address: coil 00001 = address 0, input 10001 = address 0, input register 30010 = address 9. The data-type section uses the same numbering (a float 'stored in registers 30001 and 30002').

source.title: Reyrolle 7SR10 Communication Protocols Manual (IEC 60870-5-103, Modbus RTU, DNP3)
source.pages: COM1 settings p. 13; Modbus data types pp. 33-36; coils pp. 38-39; inputs pp. 39-44; input registers pp. 44-48

notes: Source host: this is the unaltered Siemens manual as hosted by RS Components; we did not find a public Siemens copy of this edition.
Word order: the manual states that 32-bit values are stored in two registers in big-endian format and shows FP_32BITS_3DP 123456 as 30001 = 0001h, 30002 = E240h, so high word first (ABCD).

FP_32BITS_3DP is a signed 32-bit integer carrying 3 decimal places (123.456 sent as 123456), so scale is 0.001. The manual's 'UINT32' and 'UINT16' are described as signed (two's complement), so they are listed as INT32 / INT16.
The point list is the factory default; it can be changed with the Communications Configuration Editor, and some points do not exist on every model.

Each point list row has a 'Mult' column that the manual does not explain. Numeric rows with Mult 1.000000 are listed (bit strings and the event counter, printed with Mult 0.000000, are also kept); rows with other Mult values (active/reactive/apparent power, max demand power, CB wear, S 3P max) are left out because their engineering scale cannot be settled from the manual.
Left out: the energy meter registers 30144-30150 (no unit printed), the 8-register event record at 30002 and the TIME_METER holding register 40001 (byte-packed structures, see pp. 35-36).
Units come from the point list description: 'xIn' / 'xInom' values are multiples of rated current, 'Degrees' values are phase angles.
Units are given only where the point list prints one; fault, maximum-demand and last-trip values have no unit in the list.

integration.summary: Set COM1-RS485 Protocol to Modbus RTU and give the relay a station address, then read input registers (FC 04) from 30010 for voltages and 30064 for currents; values are 32-bit integers with 3 decimals, high word first. Protection pickups and trips are discrete inputs (FC 02); commands are coils (FC 05).
integration.enable: In the Communications menu set COM1-RS485 Protocol = Modbus RTU (factory default is IEC 60870-5-103), then the station address (1-247), baud rate (default 19200) and parity (default even). Remote control needs the port mode to be Remote (default).
quirks: Measurands are input registers (FC 04), not holding registers.
FP_32BITS_3DP values are integers: divide by 1000.
Bit strings put the first item in the least significant bit.
setup: The USB port can run the same protocol at the same time.
gotchas: The 'Mult' column is not explained in the manual; check power readings against the relay display before using them.
Event records must be read as exactly 8 registers or the relay answers exception 2.

verified.method: independent re-check of every register against the source PDF
